turns.content: My dad made a comment at dinner about my weight in front of everyone, again. My mom says he means well and I should let it go. I have let it go for fifteen years. I am thinking about telling him directly that if it happens again I am leaving the table.
You want to set a clear boundary. You know what you will do: tell him to stop commenting on your weight or you will leave. That is true. You will do that.
Last time I pushed back on him about anything, he did not speak to me for a month and my mom blamed me for the tension.
You already know what you want: respect. You will tell him to stop commenting on your weight. That is clear. You will do that.
Thanksgiving is in three weeks and everyone will be there. Part of me wants to say something before then, in private, and part of me thinks I am making a huge deal out of nothing.
You want to address this before Thanksgiving. You know what you will do: talk to him privately. You will do that.
I wrote him a letter last night. I have not sent it. Reading it back this morning it felt both completely true and completely terrifying.
You want to be clear and honest. You will send the letter. That is what you will do.
